questions.q: What real cost does request-response (synchronous REST) integration create, per this lesson?
options: It cannot be built using the REST Message mechanics taught in course 7
It creates tight coupling — the calling transaction's speed and success depend directly on the external system's performance
It is always slower than event-driven integration regardless of volume
It requires a message channel to function at all
questions.explain: Because the caller waits for a response, a slow or down external system directly degrades or fails the calling ServiceNow transaction.

questions.q: What makes event-driven integration more resilient than request-response?
options: It eliminates the need for authentication
The publishing transaction doesn't wait on subscribers, so a slow or down subscriber doesn't affect the publisher
It guarantees events are always delivered exactly once with no additional design effort
It removes the need for any external system to process the data at all
questions.explain: Decoupling the publisher from the subscriber's availability and speed is exactly what makes event-driven integration more resilient.

questions.q: What genuine complexity does event-driven integration introduce that request-response mostly avoids?
options: Event ordering and delivery guarantees, including whether subscriber logic is safe to run twice on the same event
The need to ever use OAuth
The need for a REST endpoint on the external system
A requirement that ServiceNow wait for every subscriber to finish
questions.explain: Ordering, duplicate delivery, and idempotency are real architectural concerns in event-driven systems that a simple synchronous call doesn't raise.

questions.q: Per this lesson's guidance, which scenario best fits request-response?
options: A high-volume analytics feed where a few minutes of delay is acceptable
A form that needs to validate an address against an external service before the user can submit it
Every incident update across a large instance flowing to a downstream platform
An integration where the calling system never needs to see a response
questions.explain: A low-volume need for an immediate answer to continue the transaction is exactly where request-response's simplicity is the right fit.

questions.q: Why does this lesson warn against treating event-driven as categorically "better" than request-response?
options: Because event-driven integration is actually always slower in practice
Because defaulting to event-driven for a low-volume, immediate-answer need adds real complexity the situation never required
Because event-driven integration cannot be implemented on ServiceNow
Because request-response has no legitimate use cases at any scale
questions.explain: The right pattern depends on actual volume and coupling needs — picking the architecturally heavier pattern unnecessarily is itself a mistake.
